member.name: T:SupplyChain.Application.Authorization.Permissions
member.summary: The complete catalogue of permissions, mirroring the legacy menu structure.

remarks.para: The VB6 application stored permissions across three tables — Sys_User_MM, Sys_User_MS and Sys_User_MSS — one row per user per menu item, at three levels of nesting, and enforced them by setting .Visible = False on menu controls.
Here a permission is a claim, checked by an authorization policy on the endpoint. Hiding a navigation link is a courtesy; the endpoint is what enforces access.

The catalogue is defined in full so that migrated legacy grants have somewhere to land. Permissions marked "not yet enforced" have no endpoint behind them until the wave that builds that module; they are still assignable, so a migrated user's access is preserved exactly.
